title: Relationships Between Type of Acquisition, The Autonomy Given to the Acquired Firm, and Acquisition Success: An Empirical Analysis

context.sample_size: 129 acquisitions (70 related, 59 unrelated), from 191 total questionnaire responses

data_sources.name: mail questionnaire to senior executives in the acquiring firm (perceptual data on autonomy, acquisition success, and relatedness)

analyses.label: Table 4 (Summary Statistics) - t-test of autonomy across related vs. unrelated acquisitions (H1)

dv.name: Autonomy given to the acquired firm management
dv.source: mail questionnaire to senior executives in the acquiring firm

key_ivs.name: Type of acquisition (related vs. unrelated)
key_ivs.measure: classified into related vs. unrelated based on manufacturing/R&D and marketing relatedness scales (Likert 5-point, 1 = very low to 5 = very high relatedness); related = both manufacturing and marketing relatedness scores in excess of 3.0, unrelated = both values less than 3.0
key_ivs.source: mail questionnaire to senior executives in the acquiring firm

analyses.label: Table 5 - bivariate regression SUCCESS = a + B(AUTON) + e, Unrelated Acquisitions subgroup (H2)

dv.name: Acquisition success
dv.measure: weighted-average composite 'acquisition success' index from respondents' assessments of acquisition impact along five performance criteria (ROI, EPS, stock price, cash flow, sales growth) on a 5-point Likert scale (1 = very unsuccessful, 5 = very successful), weighted by respondent-assigned importance scores
dv.source: mail questionnaire to senior executives in the acquiring firm

key_ivs.name: Autonomy given to the acquired firm management (AUTON)
key_ivs.measure: composite measure of total autonomy (adapted Vancil 1979 17-item scale, 5-point Likert)
key_ivs.source: mail questionnaire to senior executives in the acquiring firm

analyses.label: Table 5 - bivariate regression SUCCESS = a + B(AUTON) + e, Related Acquisitions subgroup (H3)
analyses.sample: related acquisitions subgroup (76 cases per Table 5)

dv.name: Acquisition success
dv.measure: weighted-average composite 'acquisition success' index from respondents' assessments along five performance criteria (ROI, EPS, stock price, cash flow, sales growth) on a 5-point Likert scale (1 = very unsuccessful, 5 = very successful), weighted by importance scores
dv.source: mail questionnaire to senior executives in the acquiring firm

key_ivs.name: Autonomy given to the acquired firm management (AUTON)
key_ivs.measure: composite measure of total autonomy (adapted Vancil 1979 17-item scale, 5-point Likert)
key_ivs.source: mail questionnaire to senior executives in the acquiring firm

analyses.label: Split-groups slope-comparison t-test (Arnold 1982) comparing autonomy->success beta weights across related vs. unrelated acquisitions
analyses.sample: pooled related and unrelated acquisition subgroups

dv.name: Acquisition success (difference in autonomy->success regression slopes across acquisition types)
dv.measure: t-test on the difference between raw-score beta weights (slopes of acquisition success on autonomy) estimated separately for related and unrelated acquisitions, t = (B1 - B2)/(SE^2_B1 + SE^2_B2)^(1/2), df = n1 + n2 - 4
dv.source: mail questionnaire to senior executives in the acquiring firm

key_ivs.name: Autonomy x Type of acquisition (moderation of the autonomy-success slope by related vs. unrelated)
key_ivs.measure: comparison of regression slopes across the two acquisition-type subgroups via the Arnold (1982) split-groups technique
key_ivs.source: mail questionnaire to senior executives in the acquiring firm

analyses.label: Table 2 - non-response bias t-test comparing respondents vs. non-respondents on firm sales
analyses.sample: respondent and non-respondent acquiring and acquired firms

dv.name: Firm sales revenue ($ million) of acquiring and acquired firms
dv.measure: annual sales revenue ($ million), compared via t-tests between respondent and non-respondent subsamples

key_ivs.name: Respondent vs. non-respondent status
key_ivs.measure: dichotomous indicator of whether the firm's executive responded to the questionnaire
key_ivs.source: mail questionnaire to senior executives in the acquiring firm

analyses.label: Table 3 - early vs. late respondent t-test on autonomy and acquisition performance (Oppenheim 1966)
analyses.sample: early (related n=44, unrelated n=36) and late (related n=26, unrelated n=23) respondents

dv.name: [withheld: wording matches the source]
dv.measure: 5-point Likert-type scale measures of autonomy and acquisition performance, compared via t-tests between early and late respondents
dv.source: mail questionnaire to senior executives in the acquiring firm

key_ivs.name: Early vs. late respondent status
key_ivs.measure: early vs. late respondents, late defined as responses received after the second mailing
key_ivs.source: mail questionnaire to senior executives in the acquiring firm
